lc_person: R. G. (Renate/Rena) Fuks-Mansfeld, historian at the University of Amsterdam; co-compiler of Hebrew and Judaic manuscripts in Amsterdam public collections and editor of Joden in Nederland in de twintigste eeuw.
item_person: Rena Mansfeld, also named Renate Gertrud Mansfeld; University of Amsterdam professor, 1930–2012, identified by Album Academicum record id002361.

evidence.says: LC authorizes Fuks-Mansfeld, R. G., with variants Fuks-Mansfeld, Renate and Fuks-Mansfeld, Rena. Its source notes cite Hebrew and Judaic manuscripts in ... (1973), an institutional page naming Renate Fuks-Mansfeld, and Joden in Nederland in de twintigste eeuw (2007), whose title page names Rena Fuks-Mansfeld. It links Q67197855, VIAF 39387769 and ISNI 0000000066297995.

The item labels the person Rena Mansfeld and gives aliases Renate Gertrud Mansfeld and R.G. Mansfeld. It records LC n50023721, VIAF 39387769, ISNI 0000000066297995, GND 172083532 and Album Academicum id002361; its birth and death years are 1930 and 2012, and it records employment at the University of Amsterdam in 1989–1996.

The university's own record identifies R.G. Fuks-Mansfeld, with given names Renate Gertrud and familiar name Rena, and birth and death years 1930–2012. It records a University of Amsterdam professorship in modern Jewish history and culture in 1989–1996 and the 1989 Leiden dissertation De Sefardim in Amsterdam tot 1795.
The graph's Open Library author OL903193A is named R. G. Fuks-Mansfeld.

This author's works include Hebrew and Judaic manuscripts in Amsterdam public collections and Joden in Nederland in de twintigste eeuw, matching LC's source notes, as well as De Sefardim in Amsterdam tot 1795 and Diaspora zegen of vloek?, matching the university record.

notes: The name flag reflects shortened name forms on Wikidata. LC's variants, shared identifiers, the university profile and matching works establish the same person. LC states no birth year, so there is no birth-year conflict. LC and Wikidata were checked through their structured records because their HTML pages were unavailable.
